sam.runtime: Quick heads-up — Acme’s SLA call is 10:00 PT tomorrow. they want p95=120ms, p99=220ms for chat endpoint. We need a short note on tradeoffs.
claire.eng: Noted. Current production profile (stable kernel v1 -> switched to optimized_v2 last week) shows p95 ~110ms but p99 jumped to ~310ms under their QPS mix.
miguel.ml: Repro steps: run 1k reqs with microbatch=4, kv-cache cold, long prompts (avg 1024 tokens). Profiling shows kernel switch spike at sequence step ~80 where attention kernel falls back.
claire.eng: Key datapoint: with microbatch=1 p99 drops to ~190ms but throughput halves (QPS drops ~48%). microbatch=2 gives p95 130ms p99 230ms.
lee.prod: So product ask (p95 120 / p99 220) is tight. Can we offer a tiered carve-out: default host = p95 130, p99 240; premium carve-out for Acme = tuned settings?
nana.sales: @ana.sales typo: I'm ana.sales — we need to give Acme options they can understand: recommended config + expected cost delta.
nana.sales: Acme likely to accept small throughput hit if we guarantee p99 220. What's the perf delta?
miguel.ml: Rough numbers: microbatch=1 -> QPS *0.52, cost +~1.9x tokens/sec compute. microbatch=2 -> QPS *0.72, cost +~1.3x. Also keep int8 quant path enabled; int8 adds jitter at tail in optimized_v2, we saw rare kernel fallback causing +80ms spikes.
claire.eng: Root cause: optimized_v2 uses a new fused attention kernel that misses on certain sequence lengths and falls back to a reference kernel that is memory-bound. Fallback happens when seq_len % 32 != 0 in our compiled tiling heuristic.
sam.runtime: Can we mitigate without forcing microbatch=1 for everyone? e.g., warm KV + prefix caching + small kernel heuristic tweak?
miguel.ml: Yes — two mitigations: 1) KV warmup per-client (keep a tiny hot-cache for recent prefixes) reduces the fallback frequency; 2) adjust kernel selector to prefer older kernel for seq lengths in [65..96] when QPS>threshold. Both cost a bit of throughput.
claire.eng: We ran a quick canary: microbatch=2 + kv-hot-window=3 requests + kernel-heuristic patch => p95 125ms p99 215ms, QPS ~0.68 of baseline. Repro log:
```
Request mix: 40% short, 60% long (~1k tokens)
Baseline (v1, microbatch=4): p95 110ms p99 185ms QPS=100
After optimized_v2 swap (no mitigations): p95 108ms p99 310ms QPS=102
Patch (microbatch=2 + kv-hot-window=3 + kernel-heuristic): p95 125ms p99 215ms QPS=68
```
lee.prod: That looks promising. For Acme pitch: two options: (A) Standard: run optimized_v2 default (p95~110 p99~310) cheaper but no p99 guarantee; (B) Guaranteed: apply patch + microbatch=2, kv-warmup — meets p95/p99 with ~32% throughput loss and premium pricing.
nana.sales: Can you give a one-line summary for pricing team?
claire.eng: One-liner: "To meet Acme p95=120/p99=220 we recommend microbatch=2 + small kernel-selector patch + KV warm-window; expect ~30% throughput reduction vs baseline and a ~25–35% uplift in infra cost."
perf-bot: deploy-check: kernel-selector patch passes unit tests, perf canary run shows p99 improvement 95th percentile of runs. CI perf diffs attached. :white_check_mark:
sam.runtime: Thanks — I'll prep a short doc for the customer call with the two options and the tradeoffs (latency vs throughput vs cost). If Acme wants both high throughput and strict p99 we should discuss Dedicated capacity SLA.
miguel.ml: FYI — logged follow-up issue to make fallback deterministic and add instrumentation around attention kernel hit-rate. ticket: RT-INF-3218
ana.sales: Great, thanks team. I'll sync with Acme and ask if they prefer guaranteed carve-out or try default first.
sam.runtime: Okay closing the loop here, please drop any additional perf logs below if you run more repros. :thumbsup:
